57297-veiled-women.creator: Marmaduke Pickthall
57297-veiled-women.description: A book by Marmaduke Pickthall. hook her fist at his receding shape, glass bracelets tinkling on her strong brown arm. She sighed, “The curse of God on thy religion, O thou faithless messenger!” then, with a laugh, turned round to join the group of slave-girls, her companions, sent up to lay out herbs to dry upon the roof. These had watched her invocation of the crow with knowing grins.

arxiv-2101-09534.title: Complex solutions to Maxwell’s equations Thanks: ∗ Corresponding author
arxiv-2101-09534.creator: Sachin Munshi ∗ and Rongwei Yang
arxiv-2101-09534.description: Abstract . This paper provides a view of Maxwell’s equations from the perspective of complex variables. The study is made through complex differential forms and the Hodge star operator in ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2} with respect to the Euclidean and the Minkowski metrics.

arxiv-2208-06133.title: Scholastic: Graphical Human-AI Collaboration for Inductive and Interpretive Text Analysis Conference: The 35th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology; October 29-November 2, 2022; Bend, OR, USA The 35th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST ’22)
arxiv-2208-06133.creator: Matt-Heun Hong, Lauren A. Marsh, Jessica L. Feuston, Janet Ruppert, Jed R. Brubaker, Danielle Albers Szafir
arxiv-2208-06133.description: Abstract . Interpretive scholars generate knowledge from text corpora by manually sampling documents, applying codes, and refining and collating codes into categories until meaningful themes emerge. Given a large corpus, machine learning could help scale this data sampling and analysis, but prior research shows that experts are generally concerned about algorithms potentially disrupting or driving interpretive scholarship.

arxiv-2209-08718.title: Density-aware NeRF Ensembles: Quantifying Predictive Uncertainty in Neural Radiance Fields
arxiv-2209-08718.creator: Niko Sünderhauf, Jad Abou-Chakra, Dimity Miller
arxiv-2209-08718.description: Abstract We show that ensembling effectively quantifies model uncertainty in Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) if a density-aware epistemic uncertainty term is considered. The naive ensembles investigated in prior work simply average rendered RGB images to quantify the model uncertainty caused by conflicting explanations of the observed scene.

arxiv-2503-02865.title: FairSense-AI: Responsible AI Meets Sustainability
arxiv-2503-02865.creator: Shaina Raza, Mukund Sayeeganesh Chettiar, Matin Yousefabadi, Tahniat Khan, Marcelo Lotif
arxiv-2503-02865.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce FairSense-AI : a multimodal framework designed to detect and mitigate bias in both text and images. By leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs), FairSense-AI uncovers subtle forms of prejudice or stereotyping that can appear in content, providing users with bias scores, explanatory highlights, and automated recommendations for fairness enhancements.

arxiv-2507-11649.title: ZKP-FedEval: Verifiable and Privacy-Preserving Federated Evaluation using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
arxiv-2507-11649.creator: Daniel Commey, Benjamin Appiah, Griffith S. Klogo, and Garth V. Crosby
arxiv-2507-11649.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative model training on decentralized data without exposing raw data. However, the evaluation phase in FL may leak sensitive information through shared performance metrics. In this paper, we propose a novel protocol that incorporates Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to enable privacy-preserving and verifiable evaluation for FL.

arxiv-2509-00137.title: Big bounce and black bounce in quasi-topological gravity
arxiv-2509-00137.creator: Yi Ling 1,2, Zhangping Yu 1,2
arxiv-2509-00137.description: Abstract In the framework of quasi-topological (QT) gravity, we propose a novel model which is characterized by a bounce of the spacetime such that the singularity in standard general relativity can be avoided in both cosmological and black hole setups.

arxiv-2604-12495.creator: Louis-Brahim Beaufort

pmc-10557219.title: Swallowing disorders and mortality in adults with advanced cancer outside the head and neck and upper gastrointestinal tract: a systematic review
pmc-10557219.creator: Danielle Nunes Moura Silva, Laélia Cristina Caseiro Vicente, Vanessa Laís Pontes Glória, Amélia Augusta de Lima Friche
pmc-10557219.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundAlthough oncological palliative care is increasingly being offered by multidisciplinary teams, there is still a lack of data about some symptoms handled by these teams, such as dysphagia, in patients with advanced cancer outside swallow regions.

pmc-10714025.title: The Impact of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) on Oncology: Application, Expectations, and Future Prospects
pmc-10714025.creator: Yanxing Li, Wentao Gao, Zhenhua Luan, Zhi Zhou, Jianjun Li
pmc-10714025.description: The integration of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer (ChatGPT) into the field of oncology has recently garnered significant attention, with potential implications for enhancing both research and clinical practice. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the evolving landscape of ChatGPT applications in oncology, emphasizing its contributions to diagnosis, treatment, research, and patient education.

pmc-11392178.title: A commentary on ‘A bibliometric analysis of gastric cancer liver metastases: advances in mechanisms of occurrence and treatment options’
pmc-11392178.creator: Yanlong Shi, Yizhu Wang, Kaiyi Niu, Yewei Zhang
pmc-11392178.description: t is noteworthy that these findings will serve as a valuable reference for the development of GCLM in basic and clinical research. We cordially congratulate the authors for their distinguished efforts and contributions to this field. Herein, we would like to express several constructive issues to enhance this subject.

pmc-11399863.title: Proteome-wide Mendelian randomization and single-cell sequencing analysis identify the association between plasma proteins and gastric cancer
pmc-11399863.creator: Yichen Jin, Zilong Lei, Peixin Li, Guoruiyu Lyu
pmc-11399863.description: BackgroundTargeted therapy is a crucial treatment modality for advanced gastric cancer, with several targets already identified, and the exploration of new targets is important. In this study, our aim was to identify plasma proteins causally associated with gastric cancer to explore novel genetic targets for the disease.

pmc-11452423.title: Large language models and their big bullshit potential
pmc-11452423.creator: Sarah A Fisher
pmc-11452423.description: Newly powerful large language models have burst onto the scene, with applications across a wide range of functions. We can now expect to encounter their outputs at rapidly increasing volumes and frequencies. Some commentators claim that large language models are bullshitting, generating convincing output without regard for the truth.

pmc-11519494.title: Reply to: mRNA COVID-19 vaccinations are not associated with RVO development 21 days and 12 weeks after vaccination
pmc-11519494.creator: Jing-Xing Li, Yu-Hsun Wang, Henry Bair, Shu-Bai Hsu, Connie Chen, James Cheng-Chung Wei, Chun-Ju Lin
pmc-11519494.description: We appreciate your interest in our study. This study contrasts with Dorney et al.‘s focus on the first 21 days. We conducted a re-analysis regarding selection bias and found consistent results. Our research highlights the elevated risk of retinal vascular occlusion after vaccination, which can last up to two years.

pmc-12592522.title: Comparative effectiveness of toric IOLs and LRIs for correction of moderate regular astigmatism during phacoemulsification
pmc-12592522.creator: Yiran Hu, Qianwei Zhu, Zhenni Du, Fangfang Han, Yeshuan Wu, Xiang Li, Quanyong Yi, Jianing Ying, Xiaoli Mao, Xiangxiang Fu
pmc-12592522.description: Corneal astigmatism frequently coexists with age-related cataract and may impair uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) if not addressed during surgery. Limbal relaxing incisions (LRI) and toric intraocular lenses (toric IOL) are two common methods for astigmatism correction, but evidence comparing their effectiveness in patients with moderate regular astigmatism remains limited.

pmc-13317126.title: Confident judgments of (mis)information veracity are more, rather than less, accurate
pmc-13317126.creator: Akshina Banerjee, Matthew D Rocklage, Mohsen Mosleh, David Rand, John Bellettiere
pmc-13317126.description: Does confidence help or hinder the recognition of misinformation? Prior work has reached opposing conclusions, in part because it has not separated confidence in a specific judgment from confidence in one's abilities in general. Here, we separate these constructs and test them side-by-side.

pmc-13361321.title: Genome-Wide Association Mapping and Integrated Transcriptomic-Genomic Analysis Reveal Candidate Genes for Grain Transparency in Rice
pmc-13361321.creator: Fuge Cai, Fujun Wang, Shuai Nie, Minhua Zheng, Song Bai, Hui Li, Meilin Tan, Mengquan Chen, Dilin Liu, Wu Yang

pmc-13384647.title: Elucidating the mechanism of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke: A network pharmacology and molecular docking study
pmc-13384647.creator: Tailai Shi, Zhaoqi Chen, Mengmeng Wang, Danna Chen
pmc-13384647.description: A large number of functional disorders and uncomfortable symptoms often remain following ischemic stroke (IS). Existing drug therapy is not ideal for the direct improvement of symptoms, which often leads to poor patient compliance with physical rehabilitation therapy. Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD) is a famous prescription that is effective in treating IS, especially during the sequela stage of IS.

pmc-13489403.title: Foundation models in omics research: a comprehensive survey
pmc-13489403.creator: Haozhe Liu, Wenhao Cai, Yizheng Sun, Haiping Liu, Zhiyong Zou, Qian Zhao, Sokratia Georgaka, Hongpeng Zhou, Jingyuan Sun
pmc-13489403.description: The rapid expansion of high-throughput omics has created molecular datasets of unprecedented scale and complexity. These data are rich in biological information yet inherently sparse and high-dimensional, often limiting the effectiveness of conventional machine learning techniques. Foundation models (FMs), built on large-scale self-supervised pretraining, offer a robust alternative by learning generalizable representations directly from raw biological data.
